message.content:
The crystal is described in the trigonal space group P312, number [[param:space_group.number]], with Hall symbol [[param:space_group.hall]]. Its input cell is hexagonal in character, with lattice parameters a = [[param:cell.a]] Å and b = [[param:cell.b]] Å, which share the same value, together with c = [[param:cell.c]] Å. The interaxial angles are α = [[param:cell.alpha]]°, β = [[param:cell.beta]]°, and γ = [[param:cell.gamma]]°, the last deviating only minutely from the ideal 120° of a hexagonal metric.

The input structure contains [[param:input.atom_count]] atoms in total, comprising one lithium [[param:composition.Li]], one vanadium [[param:composition.V]], and six fluorine [[param:composition.F]] atoms, consistent with a LiVF₆ stoichiometry in the unit cell.

Under the symmetry of P312, the atoms occupy three independent Wyckoff orbits. The lithium orbit [[param:orbit.o000.id]] places Li [[param:orbit.o000.element]] on the Wyckoff site [[param:orbit.o000.wyckoff]], a fixed position at 0, 0, 1/2 with multiplicity one and no free coordinates. The vanadium orbit [[param:orbit.o001.id]] places V [[param:orbit.o001.element]] on site [[param:orbit.o001.wyckoff]], fixed at 1/3, 2/3, 0, likewise of multiplicity one with no adjustable parameters. The fluorine orbit [[param:orbit.o002.id]] places F [[param:orbit.o002.element]] on the general-position site [[param:orbit.o002.wyckoff]] with coordinate relation x, y, z and multiplicity six, so its three fractional coordinates [[param:orbit.o002.parameters]] are all free. Together, the one-, one-, and sixfold orbits account for all eight atoms in the cell.

The reported frame transformation from the input to the standard setting is the identity matrix [[param:frame.matrix]] with zero origin shift [[param:frame.origin_shift]], so the input and standard coordinate frames coincide exactly, and no reorientation or origin relocation is needed to interpret the positions. Fractional coordinates from the input were rounded to [[param:round_digits]] decimal places. No precision corrections were required: the structure as given matches the idealized symmetric backbone without additional deviations, and the only departure from perfect idealization is the tiny excess of the gamma angle over 120° noted above.
